changes.after: Public_send lets code choose a method by name while respecting whether it is public.

before: respond_to?(:title) checks whether an object advertises that operation, normally excluding private methods. It is not proof of correct arguments, results, safety or authorization.

public_send invokes only a public method; send can bypass visibility, so it is not interchangeable. When a method name comes from outside the program, validate it against a fixed allowlist as well: even public methods may be inappropriate for the requested action. Here the symbol is a fixed trusted literal.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Actions
  def title
    "ready"
  end
  private
  def secret
    "internal"
  end
end
actions = Actions.new
puts actions.respond_to?(:title)
puts actions.public_send(:title)
```

Expected output or behavior: true
